concepts.name: User control of an existing notification channel
Notification permission denial and foreground services
Manual notification grouping and summary alerts

questions.prompt: On Android 8.0+, a user silences a notification channel. The app calls `createNotificationChannel()` again with the same ID and higher importance. What should the developer expect?

choices.text: Recreation deletes the old channel and all its user preferences
Recreation resets the channel to the app's requested importance
Each notification's compatibility priority overrides the channel
The app cannot override the user's channel behavior this way

questions.explanation: After creation, the app cannot change channel importance or behavior; the user controls those settings. Recreating the channel does not reset preferences, and per-notification priority is the pre-Android-8 mechanism.

sources.title: Create and manage notification channels
sources.claim: On Android 8.0+, channel importance controls interruption; after creation the app cannot change importance or channel behavior, but the user can change settings and the app can open channel settings.

questions.prompt: On Android 13+, a user denies `POST_NOTIFICATIONS`. Which statement about starting a foreground service is correct?

choices.text: Permission denial forbids every foreground service from starting
Denial removes the requirement to provide any notification for that service
Permission is not required to start it, but its notification is required
Providing the service notification automatically grants permission

questions.explanation: A foreground service does not require POST_NOTIFICATIONS to launch, but it must still include a notification and satisfy other service restrictions. Denial neither waives that notification nor auto-grants permission.

sources.title: Notification runtime permission
sources.claim: Android 13+ requires POST_NOTIFICATIONS for non-exempt notifications; denial blocks those notifications, and launching a foreground service does not require permission but still requires its notification.

questions.prompt: An Android email app manually groups independently actionable notifications and wants only the summary to alert. Which configuration matches the documented API? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Use a notification channel group instead of a summary notification
Set `GROUP_ALERT_SUMMARY` on children to suppress child alerts
Give each child a different group key to join one notification group
Mark a separate notification with `setGroupSummary(true)`
Give the children and summary the same `setGroup()` key

questions.explanation: Manual grouping uses a shared group key and an explicit summary. Children configured with GROUP_ALERT_SUMMARY leave alerts to the summary. Different keys separate groups, and channel groups organize settings rather than replacing notification groups.

sources.title: Create a group of notifications
sources.claim: Manual notification groups use setGroup with a common key and a separate summary with setGroupSummary(true); GROUP_ALERT_SUMMARY on children suppresses child alerts, and the summary ID stays constant for updates.

questions.prompt: On Android 8.0+, an app detects that its notification channel is too quiet for the user's chosen reminder behavior. What action respects the channel model?

choices.text: Set a higher compatibility priority on every new notification
Change that channel's sound programmatically after creation
Offer a link to that channel's system notification settings
Recreate that channel each time with a higher importance level

questions.explanation: The app can inspect settings and open ACTION_CHANNEL_NOTIFICATION_SETTINGS so the user can change them. It cannot override established channel importance or sound by recreation or per-notification priority.

sources.title: Create and manage notification channels
sources.claim: On Android 8.0+, channel importance controls interruption; after creation the app cannot change importance or channel behavior, but the user can change settings and the app can open channel settings.

questions.prompt: A freshly installed Android 13+ app wants to send ordinary, non-exempt notifications. What is required besides creating its notification channel?

choices.text: Add a notification group summary to bypass permission checks
Obtain the runtime `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` permission
Choose a high-importance channel to bypass permission checks
Start a foreground service to grant ordinary notification access

questions.explanation: Ordinary notifications require POST_NOTIFICATIONS on Android 13+. Importance, foreground-service use and grouping do not grant that permission or exempt ordinary notifications.

sources.title: Notification runtime permission
sources.claim: Android 13+ requires POST_NOTIFICATIONS for non-exempt notifications; denial blocks those notifications, and launching a foreground service does not require permission but still requires its notification.

questions.prompt: An Android app updates a manually grouped set of notifications. Which statements hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Give the summary and children the same notification group key
Keep the summary notification ID constant for later updates
Assign a new summary ID for every update to replace the previous one
Use `setGroupSummary(true)` on the separate summary notification
Use a different summary group key to collect all notification groups

questions.explanation: A constant summary ID updates the existing notification. The summary and children share a group key, and the summary is explicitly marked. A new ID creates another notification; a different group key separates groups.

sources.title: Create a group of notifications
sources.claim: Manual notification groups use setGroup with a common key and a separate summary with setGroupSummary(true); GROUP_ALERT_SUMMARY on children suppresses child alerts, and the summary ID stays constant for updates.
